That’s my pick. … We had open practice; we do the singing. This dude went up in the crowd, and the fans loved it. They were going crazy. … We’re all underneath the rim in the paint, and Steve (Kerr)’s going crazy. Like, ‘come on, guys,’ and he’s in the tunnel signing autographs, and Steve has to go get him. … I told him last night, I said, ‘Hey, everybody’s gonna be joking, you’re a rookie, but don’t lose that ’cause that’s actually what Steph Curry would do.'” This is remarkably high praise for a player who has yet to make his NBA debut. item.title: Micah Parsons Shares Moment With CeeDee Lamb After Cowboys-Packers Game
item.description: An injured Micah Parsons shared a moment with CeeDee Lamb following the Green Bay Packers’ victory over the Dallas Cowboys , creating a notable postgame scene between former teammates. Despite the disappointment of the 23-13 loss for Dallas, the exchange offered a reminder of the relationships that remain between players competing on opposite sides. The matchup carried added significance because Parsons, now with Green Bay, had to watch from the sidelines while dealing with an injury. The star pass rusher has been a major presence in the Packers’ defensive plans, making his absence a considerable storyline heading into the contest. His postgame greeting with Lamb showed that the rivalry between their teams did not erase their personal connection. Dec 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) during warmups prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Lamb, meanwhile, experienced a different kind of evening as Dallas attempted to compete against its former defensive standout. The Cowboys wide receiver remains one of the team’s most important offensive weapons, expected to provide production and create opportunities against opposing secondaries. Although the result went against Dallas, his encounter with Parsons became a memorable moment after the final whistle. The meeting also highlighted how quickly relationships can change in the NFL. Players who once shared a locker room and worked toward the same goals can become opponents following trades, free agency or other roster changes. When those teams meet, the competition takes center stage, but postgame interactions often reveal the mutual respect that can survive a change in uniform. item.title: Kenneth Walker III’s Hot Start Is Not Seen in Chiefs History in 24 Years
item.description: Kenneth Walker III is off to a remarkable start, producing numbers that have not been seen from a Kansas City Chiefs running back in 24 years. His early-season performance has drawn attention to his ability to take over games on the ground and potentially deliver one of the most memorable rushing campaigns in recent franchise history. Walker has emerged as a major offensive weapon, combining explosive runs with the consistency needed to keep defenses under pressure. His production has given the rushing attack a new dimension, allowing the offense to threaten opponents without depending entirely on its passing game. That balance could become increasingly important as the season progresses and opposing defenses adjust to Kansas City’s strengths. Sep 14, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III (9) scores a touchdown against the Denver Broncos during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The significance of Walker’s start becomes clearer when comparing his pace with previous performances by Chiefs running backs. The franchise has featured several productive runners over the years, but Walker’s current numbers place him in rare company. Sustaining that level of production would put him on track to challenge historical benchmarks and give the team a reliable foundation for its offensive game plan. Walker’s success also reflects the importance of establishing an effective running game early in the season. item.title: Colorado Buffaloes displaying a new belief ending into final six games
item.description: The Colorado Buffaloes may be 2-4 (0-3 Big 12), but after battling No. 11 Utah, the team seems to have found the belief it has lacked for the past month. Deion Sanders spoke Tuesday about the team's mindset after Utah and said that, despite four straight losses, the team is more together than ever. "Last week was a tremendous advancement on us showing up together," Sanders said at his weekly presser. "I don't think there were a lot of blemishes. We actially beleived coming out of the locker room for the second half that we were going to come back." Safety Randon Fontenette echoed his head coach's sentiment, saying Coach Prime's postgame approach, focusing on silver linings and telling the team how proud he was, helped immensely. "In this moment that we're in, we definitely needed that [approach] as a team," Fontenette said. "That really gelled us together and brought us together. I am very confident in these next six games." Since Saturday's game against Utah, the team has clearly shifted in attitude and mentality heading into the final six games. The Buffs saw enough against the Utes to believe they can turn their season around, with multiple wins and bowl eligibility still goals. Sanders added that he thinks the team can beat anyone in the country, but "we have to score the football." Other notes and tidbits from Deion Sanders' pre-Oklahoma State press conference Sanders does not see any quit: "I don't think you see quit in 99% of the team" On Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker: "He’s a phenomenal QB, the kid can spin it. We gotta make him uncomfortable, get him off his spots. He’s one of the best in the conference and the country." WR Danny Scudero update: "We want what is best for Danny" On QB Isaac Wilson: "He can do better than that. He knows he can’t throw that ball in that situation." On general QB struggles: "We got some guys I feel like can do that job. If they can’t that’s on us, we brought them in, nobody else, that’s on us." Micah Welch injury status: Sanders said Micah Welch is hurting and may have broken his hand. On Kam Perry's status: "I don’t know if Kam Perry is doing well; he’s still hurt. Didn’t see him today." item.title: The White House edit Donald Trump into surprising SNL sketch to mark NBA opening day
item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images The White House marked the NBA’s 2026-27 Opening Day hype by posting an edited version of an iconic SNL skit featuring President Donald Trump. The NBA is back, and the league’s slate of games on Opening Night has led to tremendous popular appeal. With fans waiting to tune back into regular season action, it’s clear that the U.S. government knows the popularity of the NBA among the voting public. As a result, the White House got involved in the hype leading to the NBA’s return to action by posting an edited SNL skit which puts the focus on the President instead of basketball. The White House edited Donald Trump into SNL’s iconic Roundball Rock segment for NBA opening day The White House shared an edited version of SNL’s ‘Roundball Rock’ skit featuring Jason Sudeikis. However, instead of posting the original skit, the White House’s version cuts to a montage of Trump and the MAGA movement instead of a performance of the iconic NBA on NBC song. President Trump previously did not associate with basketball or the NBA in his presidency until his hometown New York Knicks won the NBA Championship, with Trump becoming the first sitting U.S. President to attend an NBA Finals game with his appearance at Game 3. With Trump attending multiple sporting events over 2026, most recently appearing at a Texas vs. Tennessee CFB game, it can’t be ruled out that Trump drops in at Madison Square Garden at some point this season. Trump is not in attendance for the Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers game on opening night, which is not only the night the Knicks raised their 2026 championship banner to the rafters, but also LeBron James’ debut for the 76ers in a historic 24th NBA season. Regular season games do not get more prestigious than that, but it clearly was not worth the hassle for the President at this point in the season. He might appear in a playoff or Finals game in the summer of 2027, but right now, he will be following the Knicks’ exploits from The White House. item.title: Toprak Razgatlioglu To Miss The Rest Of The 2026 MotoGP Season
item.description: Photos by Pramac Racing. Toprak Razgatlıoğlu's MotoGP campaign has come to an early close. The Turkish rider is scheduled for shoulder surgery on October 26, in Milan, which will keep him off the grid for the remainder of the 2026 MotoGP calendar. Razgatlıoğlu injured his right shoulder in a highside crash during the Indonesian GP at Mandalika. Razgatlıoğlu flew to Milan on October 19, for a fresh round of medical checks, which confirmed the shoulder requires surgical treatment. "After further medical assessments following the crash in Mandalika, it became clear that my shoulder injury is worse than we first believed," said Razgatlıoğlu. "This wasn‘t an easy decision, but after consulting with the doctors and the people closest to me, we are convinced it is the right step for my future." Yamaha has tapped test rider Augusto Fernandez to take over the Prima Pramac Yamaha YZR-M1, starting at this weekend's Phillip Island round in Australia. As Yamaha's test rider, Fernandez already has meaningful seat time on the M1, making him the logical choice as a replacement. The timing stings for a rider who has openly relished Phillip Island throughout his World Superbike years. "I'm extremely disappointed to miss the Australian Grand Prix. Phillip Island is one of my favourite circuits and a place where I've enjoyed some very special moments during my Superbike career," Razgatlıoğlu said. "I was excited about the opportunity to race here on the MotoGP bike, which makes this situation even harder to accept." Team Director Gino Borsoi agreed that Razgatlıoğlu's long-term health is the primary concern. "We are very sorry for Toprak, as we know how much he wanted to race at Phillip Island and continue his journey with the YZR-M1," Borsoi said. "However, his health must come first, and we will support him throughout his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on the bike when he is ready." Become a Motorcycle.com insider. item.title: ‘Extremely vigilant’: NFL addresses safety concerns for Paris game amid unrest in France
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are scheduled to play the first regular-season NFL game ever held in France this Sunday. But the matchup is set to take place just days after violent protests broke out across the country, raising questions about whether the game should go on as planned. On Tuesday, a top NFL executive addressed those concerns. Peter O’Reilly said that the league is being “very vigilant” with its planning, but he insisted that it has never come close to moving or postponing the game. Unrest in France Hundreds of thousands of people took part in nationwide demonstrations across France on Saturday, protesting rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. Some of those protests turned violent, as masked groups set fires, looted shops, and attacked public buildings in several cities. Police arrested at least 1,800 people across the country, including 855 in the Paris region alone, according to the Associated Press . The game will be played at Stade de France, just north of Paris. In a statement on Saturday, the league said that preparations were continuing as scheduled and that there had been “no disruption or impact at league sites,” via ESPN . ‘We have never been close’ O’Reilly, the NFL’s executive vice president for club business and international, said that the league remains confident in its plans for Sunday. “[We’re] obviously being very vigilant in everything we do and all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with our two teams,” O’Reilly said Tuesday, via OutKick’s Armando Salguero . “We’ve got confidence in the plans both from an ops and security standpoint.” O’Reilly acknowledged that the league has contingency plans in place, including moving or postponing the game. But he said those options have never been seriously considered. “We have never been close to that point,” O’Reilly said. “As you know, we’ve always got contingency plans for every game, every single one of them. But no, we were not at that point at any point in the conversation.” O’Reilly also pointed to the league’s security team and its partnership with Stade de France, which hosted events during the 2024 Olympic Games. “Our team’s been on the ground, security team’s been on the ground, and obviously, working in close partnership with Stade de France, which is a world-class stadium, hosted world-class events, most recently the Olympic Games,” O’Reilly said. He added that security will be “heightened with local authorities” for the game. “So extremely vigilant as we always are. As I said, confident in all of those plans as we head towards Sunday,” O’Reilly said. Needless to say, the league will be keeping a close eye on the situation in France over the next few days. item.title: Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla remains confident in Jayson Tatum’s shot despite ugly 2nd half vs. Pistons
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Celtics’ Joe Mazzulla remains confident in Jayson Tatum’s shot despite ugly 2nd half vs. Pistons appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Joe Mazzulla isn’t too worried about Jayson Tatum. The Boston Celtics had a rough first game of the 2026-27 NBA season, as they squandered a big lead and lost to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, 121-113. Tatum is among the culprits behind Boston’s struggles against the Pistons, largely because of his ugly shooting, but Mazzulla would still prefer to see the star forward keep launching shots even if the rhythm isn’t there. “I just want him to continue to make the right play,” Mazzulla said of Tatum during the postgame press conference, via Celtics on CLNS. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “If he’s open, shoot it. I don’t care if he’s 0 for 10. If you’re open shoot it,” Mazzulla added. Tatum finished the game with the most minutes played among Celtics players, but only had 13 points to show. He was just 6-for-23 from the field and missed all of his seven attempts from behind the arc. While he dished out 11 assists, Boston sorely missed his scoring, especially in the second half, where the six-time NBA All-Star couldn’t find his shot, going 1-for-10 in the final 24 minutes. With Tatum misfiring, Boston newcomer and veteran forward Paul George led the way for the Celtics’ offense. George scored the most points by a player in his Celtics debut with 38 points on 12-for-21 shooting from the field. The good news for Tatum is that there is a whole lot of action ahead for the Celtics, and he could get back to his usual scoring ways as soon as Friday, when Boston welcomes the reignign NBA champions New York Knicks at TD Garden in Boston. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Knicks raised a championship banner for the first time in 53 years on Tuesday night, and they received some pretty nice jewelry, too. New York unveiled its championship ring ahead of the team's season-opener against the 76ers , a much-anticipated reveal more than four months in the making. For the Knicks, it was worth the wait. The elaborate rings wowed the Madison Square Garden crowd on Tuesday and impressed fans at home. Here's what you need to know. Knicks championship ring Here's a look at the outside and inside of the Knicks' championship ring: A WORK OF ART. @JasonofBH https://t.co/sXZEqDQ8WK — NEW YORK KNICKS (@nyknicks) October 20, 2026 The ring features the Knicks' logo on a blue background, plus the numbers of each player from the 2025-26 team wrapped around the side. The Knicks' series scores, including two 4-0 sweeps, are included on the side of the ring. The top of the ring can be twisted and lifted upward to reveal a design that resembles the exterior design of Madison Square Garden. Inside the ring is a basketball court with the Larry O'Brien Trophy at midcourt. The Knicks' championship rings not only have a tier that pulls up to look like Madison Square Garden, but it also opens to reveal the entire court and top of MSG inside. https://t.co/s36jOMFXSf — Brett Siegel (@BrettSiegelNBA) October 20, 2026 MORE : Watch the Knicks on MSG+ live with DAZN Here's the Knicks' full ring ceremony: The Knicks players get their rings in front of a raucous MSG crowd! https://t.co/HSGHJoETyC — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 20, 2026 And here's a closer look at the rings, as shown by NBC's broadcast: A closer look at the Knicks' championship ring… Just insane 🤯💍 https://t.co/LLNw7JSFjd — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 21, 2026 Here are more details about the ring. LIVE: Follow updates from Knicks vs. 76ers on opening night Knicks championship ring, by the numbers The Knicks' ring features the phrases "Knicks in Five" and "10 weeks," a reference to owner James Dolan's request for 10 weeks of sacrifice and discipline on the road to a championship. The ring also features 16 emerald-cut diamonds for each playoff win, a 0.16-carat diamond for the 16-point comeback in Game 5 of the NBA Finals, and 69 points of round white diamonds for the team's combined 69 wins between the regular season and playoffs. item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Auston Matthews joins exclusive Maple Leafs club during Blue Jackets clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Maple Leafs are off to an okay start in 2026-27. Toronto currently owns a record of 4-4-2 and are taking on the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday. For captain Auston Matthews , this is a milestone contest. As mentioned, the Toronto captain is doing his part to help the team build momentum early in the season. The wins have not followed Matthews’s production this year. If he can keep this up, though, Toronto will be a tough team to beat throughout the 2026-27 campaign. item.title: U17 Women's World Cup: Germany first to qualify for knockout stages after wins over Argentina and hosts Morocco
item.description: U17 Women's World Cup: Germany first to qualify for knockout stages after wins over Argentina and hosts Morocco Germany qualified for the knockout stages of the U17 Women's World Cup as winners of Group A. Sabine Loderer's side guaranteed their place in the Round of 16 before their final group stage fixture against bottom-placed New Zealand on Friday. The reigning European champions started their campaign with a 2-1 win over Argentina, despite conceding the opening goal inside the first ten minutes. On Tuesday, Germany sealed their qualification via the head-to-head tiebreaker after a dominant 4-2 win over hosts Morocco. Germany's best result in the competition is the third-placed finish in the inaugural tournament back in 2008. The second matchday of the U17 Women's World Cup tenth edition will continue on Wednesday with four games, including the match between former champions Japan and France.

Comedian and actor Tracy Morgan was being interviewed by the NBC Sports broadcast team and called out James on national television. Tracy Morgan: “Bronny looks like he got JUCO ball written all over him” pic.twitter.com/3alCVzDWLh — LakeShowYo (@LakeShowYo) October 20, 2026 Tracy Morgan calls out Bronny James ahead of NBA season opener between Knicks and 76ers on Tuesday night. NBAE via Getty Images “Bronny looks like he’s got JUCO ball written all over him,” Morgan said. Morgan followed up his statement on James by saying, “I just want to say what I feel. What you want?” Morgan, 57, who is a well-known, passionate Knicks fan, is watching his team play James’ father, LeBron James, who is currently playing in his first game as a member of the 76ers after he departed from the Lakers over the summer. Bronny James catches a stray from famous comedian Tracy Morgan ahead of Knicks and 76ers opener NBAE via Getty Images Before he was talking about Bronny, Morgan was saying that the Knicks are not “Scared of nobody.” While Bronny James was being scrutinized, it came after he just made the Lakers’ opening night roster, as the team elected to keep him over small forward Dalton Knecht . The decision on keeping Bronny James over Knecht came down to the wire for Los Angeles, as both of them were excused from attending Monday’s practice . Both came out of the 2024 NBA Draft, when Los Angeles selected Knecht in the first round and then took Bronny James in the second round. When Knecht first joined the team, he was regularly in the Lakers’ starting rotation, but injuries would shortly accumulate, and he was never the same. Bronny James catches a stray from Tracy Morgan ahead of Knicks vs 76ers opener. NBAE via Getty Images Bronny James has spent time back and forth between the G League and the Lakers’ active roster. Last season, he saw an increase of playing time, by appearing in 42 games and averaging 8.9 minutes per game, 2.9 points, 0.5 rebounds, and 1.2 assists. Through the preseason this year, Bronny James’ production has trended downward, scoring only 11 points in five games, while averaging 16.4 minutes per game. As the Lakers are set to usher in a new era of basketball — playing without LeBron James for the first time in eight years — the 2026-2027 season will be a make-or-break year for Bronny. The Lakers will open their season against the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night when they tip off at 7:00 p.m. PT.

item.title: Insider Reveals Michigan’s Starting QB vs. Indiana
item.description: The Michigan Wolverines appear ready to make a major change at quarterback ahead of Saturday’s matchup against No. 6 Indiana. According to new reporting, true freshman Tommy Carr is expected to start against the Hoosiers , replacing Bryce Underwood following Michigan’s dramatic comeback victory over Penn State. The development comes after head coach Kyle Whittingham confirmed Monday that Michigan had selected its starting quarterback but refused to reveal the decision publicly. Now, with multiple reports pointing toward Carr, the Wolverines appear prepared to give the freshman his first collegiate start. Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr (14) runs into the end zone for a touchdown against Penn State during the second half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Tommy Carr Expected to Start Against Indiana According to Pete Nakos’ report , Carr is expected to take over as Michigan’s starter Saturday. Additional reporting on the quarterback change also indicates the Wolverines are preparing to move forward with Carr while Underwood shifts into a backup role. Carr earned the opportunity after replacing Underwood at halftime against Penn State with Michigan trailing 3-0. The freshman completed 5 of 7 passes for 47 yards while rushing for 36 yards and a touchdown, helping the Wolverines rally for a 21-18 victory. As we previously reported , Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti had already indicated that he expected Carr to start Saturday. His assessment now appears consistent with the latest reporting surrounding Michigan’s plans. What Does This Mean for Bryce Underwood? Underwood struggled against Penn State, completing just 5 of 11 passes for 43 yards while throwing two interceptions. His difficulties protecting the football played a major role in Whittingham’s decision to make the halftime switch. As we previously detailed following Whittingham’s comments , the Michigan coaching staff wanted to evaluate both quarterbacks before choosing its starter for Indiana. That decision has apparently gone in Carr’s favor, although Whittingham has not publicly confirmed the reported selection. item.title: Max Verstappen receives fresh Formula E invitation ahead of Gen4 debut
item.description: Motorsport photo Formula E chief executive Jeff Dodds has said that he'd still love to see Max Verstappen drive the new Gen4 car, the most powerful yet used in the championship. He hasn't yet discussed it with the four-time Formula 1 champion, but he sees plenty of value if the Dutchman were to experience what the electric race car had to offer. “No, we haven’t talked to him more about the car,” Dodds told RacingNews365 . “I know he’s very focused, delighted to see him re-sign with Red Bull for the long term. And obviously, we know the team there really well, and I think they’re doing a really good job. “But I’d still love to see Max in this car, partly because I just really value his insight. So I’d love him to drive the car to be able to give us real feedback, real insight into what he thinks of it.” The Gen4 car has permanent all-wheel drive, 450kW of race power and up to 600kW in Attack Mode. And this immense power hasn't gone unnoticed, with reigning champion Lando Norris giving it a good look over during the Monaco E-Prix. Carlos Sainz and Nico Hulkenberg also had a closer look. “I forget what it’s called, Verstappen Racing, but his investments are not just in him racing Formula 1 cars,” he continued. “He’s also building academies, and he’s very focused on sim-to-track activity. "I think there are opportunities to do things with him that could be pretty exciting.” Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing In 2027, Formula E will race in Verstappen's home country for the first time with a double-header planned for Zandvoort in June. Dodds wasn't giving much away as to whether Verstappen would be involved. What he did say was that he expects the Gen4 car to entice a number of new drivers. "We’re going to be overwhelmed with potential new drivers," he said. Verstappen is certainly interested in motorsport beyond F1, as proved by his recent stint in GT racing, and has been positive in his feedback on the Gen4 cars . Maybe we'll see a crossover in the future. But for now, the United States Grand Prix awaits. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.description: ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 17: Tommy Carr #14 of the Michigan Wolverines looks to throw the ball downfield during the second half of a college football game against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Michigan Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The Michigan Wolverines won the game 21-18. (Photo by Aaron J. Thornton/Getty Images) | Getty Images As first reported by 247Sports on Tuesday night, Michigan true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr is set to make the first start of his career against the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday afternoon. Michigan is currently expected to make a change at quarterback and is currently expected to start freshman Tommy Carr at QB against No. 6 Indiana on Saturday, sources tell @CBSSports pic.twitter.com/TqHvfCdoPL — Matt Zenitz (@mzenitz) October 20, 2026 Carr was thrust into the spotlight after being called on to replace starting quarterback Bryce Underwood against Penn State, and the freshman signal-caller fueled Michigan to a 21-18 comeback win. TOMMY CARR TO THE HOUSE! 🏠 #Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr weaves through the defense for a 12-yard touchdown to take a 21-11 lead! pic.twitter.com/5VRxFSm5QZ — Charles Post (@chas_post23) October 17, 2026 The Wolverines were in complete disarray on offense — trailing 3-0 at halftime with Underwood at the helm. But that all changed when Carr entered the game and instantly provided a much-needed spark for Michigan . Carr proceeded to lead three scoring drives in the second half, highlighted by a 12-yard, game-clinching touchdown run late in the game. He completed 5-for-7 passes and compiled 83 total yards and one touchdown. Touchdown Tommy Carr! pic.twitter.com/7iCEq4fcR7 — Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) October 18, 2026 It became clear Michigan needed a change after Underwood threw two interceptions in a scoreless first half against Penn State, and Carr’s impact was palpable. Now, the freshman quarterback gets his chance to start. Prior to his appearance against Penn State, Carr only played in one other game this season. In a blowout win over UTEP, Carr completed 2-for-2 passing attempts for 23 yards and one touchdown. He also had two carries for 18 rushing yards. 14 ➡️ 12 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/6Mh1krAIOm — Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) September 19, 2026 The 6-foot-4, 195-pound quarterback is the grandson of legendary former Michigan head coach Lloyd Carr, who led the program to the 1997 national championship. Nearly three decades later, his grandson will start for the very first time against the reigning national champions.

item.title: Colin Cowherd denounces Junior Caminero’s home run trot: ‘That was obnoxious’
item.description: Credit: FS1 Tampa Bay Rays superstar Junior Caminero is making baseball fun again, but Colin Cowherd is the fun police. Caminero had his moment Monday night, hitting a monster seventh-inning home run off Cleveland Guardians closer Cade Smith that all but punched Tampa’s ticket to the World Series. The towering blast gave the Rays a 5-1 lead, and they won Game 6 of the ALCS 7-3 to advance to their third World Series in franchise history. Perhaps more notable than the homer, however, is that Caminero took 38 seconds to round the bases. Caminero stopped several times to pose and pound his chest in celebration because, well, it was the biggest hit of his career. Baseball purists have waved the white flag on a pitch clock; they’ve let the DH into the National League; they’ve even allowed some semblance of celebrating on the field, but Colin Cowherd and others still are not ready to see a player take 38 seconds to trot around the bases. “I think baseball sometimes needs to lighten up, that is way over the top rounding first… I’m all for flexing, that was obnoxious.” – Colin Cowherd on Junior Caminero’s home run trot https://t.co/H73MRXtpg0 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 20, 2026 “I am for celebrating; I think baseball sometimes needs to lighten up,” Cowherd admitted. “That is way over the top rounding first. Baseball for years was like, ‘There’s a way to play the game,’ and everybody else had a different idea on the way to play the game. But right before he got to home plate, he stopped, I thought, ‘Oh, this is obnoxious.’ Two things can be true: I’m all for flexing; that was obnoxious. It’s his style. He’s a bit over the top, it felt obnoxious to me.” Rip players for celebrating after hitting a solo home run that made the score 8-2 in an elimination game . Mock teams for wearing goggles and popping champagne every time they clinch something . If this happened in the first inning of a June game, Cowherd would have a point. But when a home run essentially sends your team to the World Series, let the player take 38 seconds to flex. item.title: “That’s a Really Lame Take”: Kentucky HC Will Stein Defends New 24-Team College Football Playoff Format
item.description: Will Stein & Kentucky Wildcats Football © Instagram/@coachwillstein As the College Football Playoff is expected to expand from a 12- to 24-team format starting with the 2027 postseason, the college football fraternity seems divided on the concept. One of the biggest areas of concern for those against the expansion is the importance of regular-season matchups. With an increased number of teams set to qualify for the CFP, programs would have a bigger margin of error to play with, which could result in a decrease in the weight of the regular-season games. However, Will Stein begs to differ. The Kentucky Wildcats coach, according to On3 Sports , defended the proposed expansion, dismissing concerns that a 24-team playoff would reduce the significance of regular-season games. “Everybody says the (regular season) games aren’t going to matter. Really? I think that’s a really lame take, to be honest. As far as I know, every game in College Football is going to matter,” Stein said. “You telling me you wouldn’t want a Playoff game at Kroger Field? I think those takes are bad.” On the field, the Kentucky Wildcats (6-1, 4-1 SEC) are tied for first place in the SEC with No. 5 Georgia (6-1, 4-1) and are ranked No. 12. ESPN Reportedly Agrees To Pay $345 Million Annually For Expanded CFP While the college football world argues whether the expansion of the College Football Playoff is the right step for the sport, the format change appears to be a major financial deal for college football. With reports of a handshake agreement between CFP and ESPN to broadcast the 24-team playoff format starting in 2027, Pete Thamel reported that ESPN will pay the CFP $345 million annually for the next five years. However, ESPN will earn back $140 million due to the cancellation of three power conference championship game agreements. These annual broadcasting fees will be paid on top of a $1.3 billion sum that the network is already slated to pay the CFP as part of its existing college football broadcasting rights. item.title: Buckeye Backups Set to Battle for the Ohio State Starting QB Job
item.description: If there is a silver lining to be found in this entire Julian Sayin situation, it is that it happened during the bye week, so the Ohio State Buckeyes have some time to get their ducks in a row. The bad part, amongst many bad parts about this injury is that the first start for either Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair is going to get their first start on the road against the USC Trojans in a primetime slot. The environment is going to be massive, and the challenge is going to be large for whoever it may be. While we have seen Fahey first up in each of the games this season, Ryan Day said that there will be a competition this week to find next week's starter. After releasing the news that Sayin was likely going to miss the remainder of the season, he said that the bye week is going to be an open competition for the two young players. Fahey had gotten the first opportunities because, up until this point, he had shown the Buckeyes' staff more than St. Clair had. That will still be the case, and Fahey is going to have the lead going into the bye week, but the competition is on for those two players. Instant Analysis: Ohio State Rolls to Solid Victory on the Back of Jeremiah Smith Ohio State rolled to a smoother victory over the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday afternoon. The mission was very clear: try to get the run game going, get mor... One thing is for sure: whoever gets the nod as the quarterback is going to be in great hands, with Ryan Day creating the game plan for the first start. This is where a guy like Arthur Smith, as the offensive coordinator, is going to have to lean heavily on Day's experience. I think back to week one of the 2025 season when the Texas Longhorns came to Columbus against the Buckeyes' freshman starter, Julian Sayin. One thing that Day said after the game is still ringing through my head a full year later. He said that it didn't matter what happened in that game. The only important thing was that the Buckeyes had one more point than the Longhorns. He didn't care how many yards he threw for, how many touchdowns, or how many completions. All that mattered was one more point than Texas. They got it that day, and that's the message next week against the USC Trojans. It doesn't matter who scores the touchdowns or how it happens. Next week, only one thing matters: scoring one more point than the USC Trojans. Whoever is going to get the nod under center will have to earn it this week as they battle it out.

The NFL is not punishing the Eagles for the handling of Hurts, who was cleared to play before Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after he was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf. READ MORE | Jalen Hurts out for season after blood clots discovered in Eagles QB's lungs Hurts, 28, is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs days after the game. item.description: Fire, noise, fury, a sense of empty energy. And across town, a football match too. Do any of these randomly pitched autumnal Champions League fixtures mean anything? Probably not when you’re Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona, and the only game in town is risk-free TV income and a semi-guaranteed place in the knockout stuff. But this was still a dazzling occasion at the Parc des Princes, where the champions of France and Spain played out a light, open, frictionless, exhibition-style game of football. PSG finished 4-2 winners, having been pegged back to 2-2 midway through the second half. But this was also a game where the score almost did not seem to matter, and where the only really hard message was the frailty of the Barcelona backline and PSG’s thrilling attacking energy in these midweek A-games. item.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal
item.description: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum. Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez. item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
